name: Copilot CLI
note: GitHub Copilot's command-line agent, which is a different thing from the VS Code extension the `copilot` harness charts quota for and the `vscode` harness reads sessions from. It keeps its own SQLite store at ~/.copilot/session-store.db with a row per session and a usage event per model call, so token counts come from the agent's own accounting rather than from re-parsing a transcript. Cache reads are summed separately from input, because they are re-used server-side rather than uploaded again.

installationProbes.method: collision: the language server, not the agent
installationProbes.name: copilot-language-server

compatibility.note: Read from the CLI's own SQLite store; validate against a local install with --check.

source.query: SELECT s.id AS sessionID, s.cwd AS cwd, s.summary AS title, s.updated_at AS lastActivity, s.created_at AS startedAt, (SELECT u.model FROM assistant_usage_events u WHERE u.session_id = s.id ORDER BY u.id DESC LIMIT 1) AS model, (SELECT SUM(u.input_tokens) FROM assistant_usage_events u WHERE u.session_id = s.id) AS inputTokens, (SELECT SUM(u.output_tokens) FROM assistant_usage_events u WHERE u.session_id = s.id) AS outputTokens, (SELECT SUM(u.cache_read_tokens) FROM assistant_usage_events u WHERE u.session_id = s.id) AS cacheRead, (SELECT SUM(u.cache_write_tokens) FROM assistant_usage_events u WHERE u.session_id = s.id) AS cacheWrite, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM turns t WHERE t.session_id = s.id) AS turns FROM sessions s ORDER BY s.updated_at DESC LIMIT 200
